shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index fell on Wednesday, after rising to a one-week high in the previous session, weighed down by weaker rates in the capesize vessel category.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index fell on Wednesday, after rising to a one-week high in the previous session, weighed down by weaker rates in the capesize vessel category.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, was down 2 points, or 0.06%, at 3,430 points
The capesize index (.BACI) fell 31 points, or 0.5%, to 5,861 points.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, decreased by $286 to $49,652.

Iron ore futures edged up, continuing to stabilise after last week's sharp fall, as supply disruption in Brazil linked to El Niño provided short-term support, countering a drag from weak Chinese steel mill profitability.
The panamax index (.BPNI) rose 34 points, or 1.5%, to 2,333 points.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, gained $309 to $20,996.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index (.BSIS) inched up 2 points, or 0.1%, to 1,778.
